body:
Lot’s of controversy at this tournament surrounding

the prize of the not yet released foil japanese vader.



it was given as a raffle of sorts with first place getting

the best chance to win and last place getting a chance,

it ended up going to 5th place.



anyways.  i get up, head to mc’donalds and buy

two breakfast buritos, end up at the card shop

at 9 am.  mike crawford(5th place) and little brian

green are there, i buy brian an oj, and james t arrives,

we are allowed inside moments later.



the whole crew arrives, and at about 10:05 we

begin the tournament.



ROUND 1 GAME 1



my light side ebo against Zach Stenerson’s Hunt Down.



my light is a version of deadbolt.  used prep’d defenses

for strike planning, battle plan, and insurrection.

started mpg and include 3rd marker for later.



i don’t remember what zach started with, but i knew

that I would have to get my ebo up, and drains up.



i grab crix, deploy him to war room, and start grabbing

scouts, geezum grabs extra sites and ketwol finishes

up my three, i have ebo up in 2nd round.



i win some battles in space and pull off legendary,

other stuff happened too, but eventually, I win by 9.



I would like to add more detail, but for the life of me

the shock of beating zach is too much.



highs, beating zach

lows, can’t think of any.



ROUND 1 MATCH 2



My tie deck against brian herold’s agent’s deck.



i slap him around, and well, my tournament report is sucking.







the moral of the story is, I beat zach twice, and

brian herold once and lost to him once I got third!
title: Fargo ND 1-6-01
author: Jeff Kasper
event_desc: a tournament at a card shop in Fargo, North Dakota, with a not-yet-released Japanese foil Vader raffled as a prize

games.opponent_objective: Hunt Down And Destroy The Jedi / Their Fire Has Gone Out Of The Universe
Agents In The Court / No Love For The Empire
games.note: 'i slap him around'; result inferred from the closing line (beat Herold once)
not described; from the closing line 'I beat zach twice'
not described; from the closing line '...and lost to him once'

decks.description: EBO, a version of Deadbolt (Prepared Defenses for Strike Planning, Battle Plan and Insurrection; Main Power Generators start)

summary: Jeff Kasper finished 3rd at a Fargo, North Dakota tournament on 6 January 2001 with an EBO deck and a TIE deck, beating Zach Stenerson twice and splitting two games with Brian Herold (3–1).
notes: Event: store tournament at a card shop in Fargo with no name; named 'January 2001 Fargo tournament' after [[December 2000 Fargo tournament]]. Date from the title (1-6-01). Player count not stated.
Format Premiere - Jabba's Palace Sealed Deck: 6 January 2001 is before Reflections II's release (10 January 2001).

Only two games are described ('Round 1 Game 1', 'Round 1 Match 2'); the closing line says he beat Zach twice and Brian Herold once and lost to him once, so four games (3–1) are recorded; the order and sides of the other two are not given.

Herold's 'agent's deck' is Light (Kasper plays his TIE deck); linked to Agents In The Court, the only Agents objective legal before Reflections II (Agents Of Black Sun is a Dark Reflections II objective).
EBO (Echo Base Operations) is an Effect, so no objective link for Kasper's Light deck.

Mike Crawford '5th place' (the raffled foil Japanese Vader went to 5th place). Zach Stenerson, Brian Herold and Mike Crawford linked to existing pages by the name rule. 'little brian green' and 'james t' are mentioned without results.
No live deck page for this EBO deck: [[Jeff Kasper kazper's hidden ebo v 1 6]] (1 January 2001) starts Hidden Base, not Main Power Generators, so it is not linked.
